html:
On 23 August 1989 about two million people joined hands in a human chain some 675 kilometres long, running from Tallinn through Riga to Vilnius.

The date was the fiftieth anniversary of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, whose secret protocol had handed the Baltic states to the Soviet Union. The popular fronts of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania organised the chain to demand that Moscow admit the pact and its results.

It was one of the largest peaceful protests ever seen and drew world attention. That December the Soviet government admitted the secret protocol existed. Within two years all three countries were independent. It was a high point of the Singing Revolution, and the image of a peaceful chain was copied elsewhere. See Latvia and Lithuania.
sum: On 23 August 1989 about two million people joined hands in a human chain some 675 kilometres long, running from Tallinn through Riga to Vilnius.
